'''Yeshimabeit "Yeshi" Milner''' is an American technologist and activist.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|date=2018-06-22|title=Yeshimabeit "Yeshi" Milner|url=https://equaljusticesociety.org/mindscience/speakers/yeshimilner/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Equal Justice Society|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=D'Ignazio |first1=Catherine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x5nSDwAAQBAJ |title=Data Feminism |last2=Klein |first2=Lauren F. |date=2020-03-17 |publisher=MIT Press |isbn=978-0-262-04400-4 |pages=206 |language=en}}</ref> She is the executive director and co-founder of ''[[Data for Black Lives]]''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Roose|first=Kevin|date=2020-12-30|title=The 2020 Good Tech Awards|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/30/technology/2020-good-tech-awards.html|access-date=2021-01-16|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=9 Black Women in Data Science to Know {{!}} Built In|url=https://builtin.com/data-science/black-women-data-science|access-date=2022-01-02|website=builtin.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Yeshimabeit Milner grew up in [[Miami]], [[Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Cocco|first1=Federica|last2=Smith|first2=Alan|date=July 22, 2020|title=Race and America: Why Data Matters|url=https://www.ft.com/content/156f770a-1d77-4f6b-8616-192fb58e3735|url-access=limited|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Financial Times|publisher=The Financial Times Limited}}</ref><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Lo|first=Puck|date=2018-05-30|title=Practitioner Profile: Yeshimabeit Milner|url=https://morethancode.cc/2018/05/30/practitioner-profile-yeshimabeit-milner.html|access-date=2021-01-16|website=#MoreThanCode}}</ref> Starting in her late teens, Milner became involved in activism and data science.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-07-31|title=2019 Speakers|url=https://isgmh.northwestern.edu/speakers/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Institute for Sexual and Gender Minority Health and Wellbeing (ISGMH)|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Yeshimabeit Milner on Abolish Big Data and Data 4 Black Lives|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/igsf/channels/event/yeshimabeit-milner-abolish-big-data-and-data-4-black-lives-326377|access-date=2021-01-16|work=IGSF|publisher=McGill University|archive-date=2021-01-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122012203/https://www.mcgill.ca/igsf/channels/event/yeshimabeit-milner-abolish-big-data-and-data-4-black-lives-326377|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Databite No. 129: Abolish Big Data|url=https://datasociety.net/library/abolish-big-data/|access-date=2022-01-02|website=Data & Society|language=en-US}}</ref> She worked with the ''Power U Center for Social Change'' as a high school senior.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Yeshimabeit "Yeshi" Milner|url=https://www.netrootsnation.org/profile/yeshimabeit-milner/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Netroots Nation|language=en-US}}</ref> Milner attended [[Brown University]], graduating in 2012 with a BA degree in [[Africana studies|Africana Studies]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Rosenfeld|first=Maia|date=2019-02-21|title=University event highlights complexities of data power|url=https://www.browndailyherald.com/2019/02/21/data-can-influence-inequalities-panelists-say/|access-date=2021-01-16|work=Brown Daily Herald}}</ref><ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
In 2013 at age 22, after returning to Miami after college, Milner started working with the ''Power U Center for Social Change'' and looking at Black infant mortality rates locally in trying to understand why they were disproportionately so high.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=December 11, 2019|others=Ashoka|title=Why We Need Data For Black Lives|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/ashoka/2019/12/11/why-we-need-data-for-black-lives/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":5" /> They were able to retrieve data from 300 mothers, and as a result changed local policy.<ref name=":3" />{{third-party inline|date=January 2022}}

One of her classmates at Brown University was mathematician Lucas Mason-Brown, together they founded Data for Black Lives in November 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Profile: Data for Black Lives|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/data-for-black-lives/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Predictive policing algorithms are racist. They need to be dismantled.|url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2020/07/17/1005396/predictive-policing-algorithms-racist-dismantled-machine-learning-bias-criminal-justice/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=MIT Technology Review|language=en}}</ref> The Data for Black Lives (D4BL) annual conference was started in 2018 by Yeshimabeit Milner and Lucas Mason- Brown.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Miller|first=Sandi|date=December 13, 2017|title=Calculating the cost of tech-fueled discrimination|url=https://news.mit.edu/2017/mit-data-for-black-lives-conference-calculates-cost-of-tech-driven-discrimination-1213|access-date=2021-01-17|website=MIT News, Massachusetts Institute of Technology|language=en}}</ref> They use the slogan, "Abolish Big Data!" with hopes to redesign big data and to "put data into the hands of those who need it most".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Donovan|first=Joan|date=2020-01-14|title=Redesigning consent: big data, bigger risks|url=https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/big-data-bigger-risks/|journal=Harvard Kennedy School Misinformation Review|language=en-US|volume=1|issue=1|doi=10.37016/mr-2020-006|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Kilgore |first=James |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QzMWEAAAQBAJ |title=Understanding E-Carceration: Electronic Monitoring, the Surveillance State, and the Future of Mass Incarceration |date=2022-01-18 |publisher=The New Press |isbn=978-1-62097-615-9 |pages=193 |language=en}}</ref> In 2020, the group was able to compile state-level data about the impact of COVID-19 on Black people and are working on compiling a nationwide database of technologies used by police departments.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Roose|first=Kevin|title=The 2020 Good Tech Awards|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2020/12/31/the-2020-good-tech-awards/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=baltimoresun.com|date=31 December 2020 }}</ref> In 2021, Milner co-wrote a research piece for [[Demos (U.S. think tank)|Demos]] on [[Algorithmic bias|algorithmic racism]] from [[Big Tech]] companies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Data Capitalism and Algorithmic Racism|url=https://www.demos.org/research/data-capitalism-and-algorithmic-racism|access-date=2021-12-14|website=Demos|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-11|title=The Capitalist in the Machine: Decoding Data Capitalism|url=https://nonprofitquarterly.org/the-capitalist-in-the-machine-decoding-data-capitalism/|access-date=2021-12-27|website=Nonprofit Quarterly|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards and accolades ==
Milner served on the board of the [[Highlander Research and Education Center]] in Tennessee.<ref name=":4" /> In 2018, she was awarded a Roddenberry Foundation Fellowship, which honors and invests in extraordinary people who can change the world.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Yeshimabeit Milner|url=https://roddenberryfoundation.org/blog/fellow/yeshimabeit-milner/|access-date=2021-02-21|website=Roddenberry Foundation|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2020, Data for Black Lives and its founders were awarded the [[Forbes 30 Under 30]] and the New York Times 2020 Good Tech Awards.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=30 Under 30 2020: Social Entrepreneurs|url=https://www.forbes.com/30-under-30/2020/social-entrepreneurs/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref>
